headline: Eagles in the Arena: After state title loss, Bakersfield Christian HS looks to right the wrongs of the past
content:
The Daily Brief

Eagles in the Arena: After state title loss, Bakersfield Christian HS looks to right the wrongs of the past

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 14, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a look at the night that was — from a high-speed DUI south of the Grapevine to a welfare check for a woman seen crying for help in a red pickup. Today’s high will reach 95°, with an overnight low around 67°, and air quality is moderate at AQI 59. Let’s get you caught up.

The Kern Overnight

The night opened quietly enough, with a traffic unit requested around 9:10 p.m. for the 600 block of 33rd Street. But by 9:23 p.m., dispatchers were sending city units to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking the eastbound roadway. The incident drew no further update on the air. Around 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street; officers took the report, and no arrests were announced. The night’s most serious call came around 11:34 p.m., when Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver’s window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound, and the broadcast went out citywide. Fire crews were comparatively quiet, handling a residential alarm on Greenview Lane around 11 p.m. that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion, and rescue unit before the air went quiet. Just after midnight, a theft from a space at a mobile home park on Barlow Road was reported, with a loss estimated near $3,900 and a suspect named. And shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park saw a burgundy Freightliner hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim as the feed moved on.

Today's weather

Today’s high will reach 95° under sunny skies, with a low tonight around 67°. It’s currently 77° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at AQI 59.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team is looking to right the wrongs of last year’s state title loss as they gear up for the new season. The Eagles are working to build on their experience and come back stronger, with a focus on teamwork and determination.

23ABC tells us that Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works.

23ABC also shares that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego on August 12 to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

KGET 17 reports that Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region’s industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California’s current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of the $109 million federal aviation funding. This funding will support improvements and upgrades to local airport infrastructure.

Coming up this week

This afternoon, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1 p.m., followed by the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee at noon and the Special Laws and Legislation Committee at noon. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon, the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4 p.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And this weekend, the Fox Theater will host PEPPER With CYDEWAYS on August 14, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.

headline: STEM in Kern: Understanding recent major earthquakes
content:
The Daily Brief

STEM in Kern: Understanding recent major earthquakes

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 15, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a reminder of the Eagles’ resolve. Today’s top story follows Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team as they regroup after a state title loss. We’re looking at a high of 95° and a low of 69°, with clear skies and good air quality. Let’s see what happened overnight and what the day holds.

The Kern Overnight

A night that opened with a road-rage pair stalling traffic on White Lane and closed with a stolen van on Kentucky Street and a fender dispute between big rigs at the Flying J. Law enforcement carried most of the load: a 90-plus mph DUI south of the Grapevine, a reported theft from a mobile home park on Barlow Road, and the night's most serious call — an attempt-to-locate after a woman was seen crying for help out the window of a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace. Fire crews were comparatively quiet: a residential alarm that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion and rescue unit before the air went quiet.

Around 11:34 p.m., Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver's window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound. It's the kind of call dispatchers don't sit on: no description of plates or direction of travel beyond southbound, so the broadcast went out citywide for any unit to catch the truck. No further update was heard on the air before the feed moved on.

headline: 3 dead after wrong-way crash on Highway 99 near Bakersfield, CHP says
content:
The Daily Brief

3 dead after wrong-way crash on Highway 99 near Bakersfield, CHP says

Good morning Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16th, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm start to the day with temperatures already in the low 80s. Today’s top story is a tragic wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that claimed three lives overnight. We’ve also got a moderate air quality day ahead, with no active weather alerts for Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded just before 1 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a vehicle fire and extrication drew a heavy response. Crews worked to free a pinned, unconscious subject from a vehicle, ultimately pulling two patients out as green tags. Around the same time, a DUI driver fled eastbound from the 33rd Street area in a white BMW 5 Series. Earlier in the evening, a palm tree fire climbed into the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way off Villalobos Street, drawing a reinforced alarm with Engine 7 as incident commander. Units also staged on Price Street around 9:48 p.m. for a possible shooting that never developed on the air, and handled a long string of domestics and disturbances — including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a wall was punched. Shortly before 5:40 a.m., one vehicle struck a parked car at Myrtle Avenue, drawing multiple engine companies and Battalion 4 for a patient assessment.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 82° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is holding at a moderate AQI of 58.

Top stories

23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning. According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado at around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire. CHP says all 3 occupants inside the vehicle died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the 2 occupants in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries. Officials say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with significant injuries and even fatalities reported. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works to deter illegal fireworks use.

23ABC shares that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos said one of the most debated topics during the two-day Washington meeting was how long recovery should last, pushing back on the view that recovery should only be for a treatment program of 28 days.

Kern County is making a mark on the national stage this week. Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. This initiative highlights local expertise contributing to broader solutions for addiction challenges.

The Daily Brief

Fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield

All were described as wearing dark clothing, and though no shots were fired, units were responding as the feed moved on. Earlier, shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and looking for a suspect vehicle, though the exact location was unclear on the air. Fire crews also handled a one-acre grass fire near the bike path off Oak Street just after 10:30 p.m., with a slow rate of spread. In other incidents, multiple units responded to a domestic violence call in progress on Animas Court at 9:54 p.m., and an ex-boyfriend reportedly smashed a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue around 11:03 p.m. The small hours ran quieter, with the usual spread of disturbances, medical aids, and welfare checks.

The move highlights the close working relationship between local law enforcement and the DA’s office, and it’s expected to bring a wealth of experience to the role.

23ABC reported on Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs sharing their Fourth of July findings at a recent meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., to develop the toolkit with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the Department of Health and Human Services. It’s a proud moment for Kern County to be at the forefront of such important work.

headline: Kern County Sheriff’s Office warns of scammers impersonating KCSO employees
content:
The Daily Brief

Kern County Sheriff’s Office warns of scammers impersonating KCSO employees

The Kern Overnight A truck fire that tipped over and burned down a trailer west of Bakersfield escalated into a wildland response around 9:47 p.m., drawing multiple engines, a dozer, helicopter 409 and a water tender. Crews worked to access the burn after the reporting party pointed out lights on the hill. Just before 3:45 a.m., a 53-foot trailer north of Pond on Garzoli Road was fully involved, with a spot of grass fire spreading alongside it. Battalion crews responded to what dispatch dubbed the Garzoli Incident and remained on scene for hotspots. Just before 10:45 p.m., a caller reported about 30 shots fired, mostly in a field in the area of Panama Lane & South Allen Road. The call stood for service while units investigated. Around 3:06 a.m., a welfare check near the Wells Fargo on Columbus Street escalated — a man on a bicycle was approached by subjects and an impact sound was heard, followed by a fight involving three people. Two suspects fled northbound Columbus; units searched. Just after 4 a.m., a big-rig incident with a load of table grapes brought a roadway closure in Delano, with Environmental Health notified.

Today's weather Expect a high near 98° and a low around 73° tonight. It's currently 95° at Meadows Field (KBFL). A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect until 11:00 p.m. tonight. Air quality is 112 — unhealthy for sensitive groups.

Top stories **KGET 17 reports that** the Trump administration's push to rescind protection on forested areas could have Kern County impact. **KGET 17 said that** the Shafter City Council will discuss a proposed ordinance banning sleeping in public places. **23ABC tells us that** a 21-year-old woman was arrested in a deadly South Bakersfield stabbing. Officers responded to a home in the 400 block of White Lane around 3:30 p.m. Monday, where they found a man who had been stabbed. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Homicide detectives investigated and arrested Erionna Russel, 21, on suspicion of second-degree murder. Police say Russel and the victim knew each other. Russel is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. The victim's identity has not yet been released. **KGET 17 announced that** a California City man was arrested after the seizure of hundreds of pounds of narcotics and a firearm. **23ABC said that** California is holding firm on school vaccine rules as national rates dip. New CDC data shows kindergarten vaccination rates are slipping across the country, raising questions about how many children are starting school without all of their required shots. National vaccination coverage among kindergarteners fell by 0.1% for all reported vaccines during the 2025-26 school year. At the same time, exemptions from one or more vaccines rose to 4.2%, up from 3.6% the year before. The CDC says about 280,000 kindergarteners nationwide went into the 2025-26 school year without documentation of completing the MMR series. The report follows Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s visit to Kern County, where he described vaccine hesitancy as part of a broader crisis of public trust. "If the public does not trust the public health agencies, we are not going to have public health," Kennedy said. The latest CDC data show California's kindergarten MMR rate at 95.7%. According to the state's 2024-25 data, Kern County's overall immunization rate was 85.4%, which included virtual schools. When looking at classroom-based schools, that rate rises to 93.7%, similar to the state average. Kern Public Health says virtual schools may be exempt from immunization requirements. California law requires children entering TK through 12th grade to have documentation of required vaccinations. Unlike many states, California does not allow religious or personal-belief exemptions. Some students can still be admitted conditionally while they complete their vaccine series. Schools are required to follow up with families, and if a child does not come into compliance, they may be excluded from school. **23ABC announced that** the fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield continues. Buck Owens' Crystal Palace closed about a year ago, and its future remains uncertain. Now, one offer on the table would mean tearing it down. Country singer Scotty Crabtree started visiting the Palace in 1999. He says performing with its house band years later helped launch his career. "Basically, my professional career started in 2007 through getting to perform with the house band at the Crystal Palace," Crabtree said. Buck Owens opened the Crystal Palace in 1996, creating a home for the Bakersfield Sound. When Crabtree learned one offer could lead to demolition, he says he couldn't sit back and watch the Palace disappear. He started an online petition that has now gathered more than 200 signatures. The Buck Owens Private Foundation confirms it has received several offers — including one still on the table that would tear the building down. In a written statement, foundation representative Jim Shaw said the hope is to find a buyer who will reopen and reimagine the venue. "Since the listing and closing of the Crystal Palace last year we've had quite a bit of interest and several offers (including one still on the table that would be a tear-down!!). Our hope is that sooner rather than later the right person will step forward with a plan to reopen the venue in a manner that will bring our beautiful building back to life. Although in our perfect world the theme would remain Buck and the Bakersfield Sound, we accept that the new iteration might not resemble the version that we all remember. There are numerous ways that the venue could be reimagined, and we are open to all serious offers." **Bakersfield Now announced that** a DUI checkpoint & saturation patrol in Bakersfield ended in two arrests and seven citations.
